verdict.rationale: Make documents an official MCP server that lets AI systems like Claude and ChatGPT 'view and modify scenarios' and 'manage the contents of your Make account'. Its first-party Make Skills are Markdown files that help an assistant with 'building scenarios, configuring modules'. Together these let a user create or edit workflows through natural-language prompts, but only via an external AI client; there is no evidence of a native prompt-to-scenario builder inside Make. Missing for 10: native in-product natural-language scenario generation/editing, hands-on or independent corroboration of prompt-driven scenario building quality, documented depth of what the MCP management tools can create versus modify.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can generate or edit a workflow from a natural-language prompt

citations.quote: Make Skills are Markdown files that help your assistant reliably perform Make-specific tasks, including building scenarios, configuring modules, and connecting to Make MCP server or third-party services.
View and modify scenarios and their related entities (e.g., connections, webhooks, and data stores)
Make MCP server allows AI systems, such as large language models (LLMs), to run scenarios and manage the contents of your Make account.
